name: Salem witch trials
hook: Nineteen hangings, spectral evidence and a panic that gave America its favorite metaphor for hysteria.

facts.statement: The Salem witch trials were 1692 proceedings in colonial Massachusetts, retold in novels such as The Heretic's Daughter.

facts.label: the hangings
facts.statement: The last witchcraft executions in Salem were on September 22, 1692. John Willard, accused by his in-laws, was hanged earlier, on August 19.

facts.label: ergot poisoning
facts.statement: Some attribute the Salem accusations to ergot poisoning, which can cause psychotic effects.

facts.label: The Crucible
facts.statement: Arthur Miller's 1953 play The Crucible is about the Salem witch trials; he researched it in Salem at the courthouse and Witch House.

facts.label: Cotton Mather
facts.statement: Cotton Mather, a Puritan minister, wrote The Wonders of the Invisible World about the trials; he and his father denounced spectre evidence.

facts.label: Nathaniel Hawthorne
facts.statement: Nathaniel Hawthorne was born in Salem in 1804 and worked at its Custom House; he wrote about it in The Scarlet Letter's introduction.

facts.label: The House of the Seven Gables
facts.statement: Hawthorne's 1851 novel The House of the Seven Gables is set in Salem and inspired by a 1668 house and a family curse.
associations: The House of the Seven Gables
